sections.heading: 4. Keep adjacent plays inside real economic boundaries
paragraphs: The mapped play sportsbook_promo_ev_matched_betting_syndicates belongs in a contract review, not in an assumption that promotional betting produces affiliate profit. State requirements differ: confirm the relevant gaming regulator's affiliate registration or licensing rules, permitted compensation structure, and operator authorization before serving that jurisdiction. A merchant's own license does not establish the publisher's status. CPA pays for a defined qualified customer; gaming revenue share depends on contract-defined net gaming revenue, deductions, and possibly negative carryover. A losing revenue-share month can offset later positive earnings where the contract allows it. Track that balance separately from customer refunds. Self-referrals, duplicate identities, coordinated bonus exploitation, prohibited incentivized traffic, and other promo-abuse indicators can trigger scrubs or termination. Do not build a forecast around defeating those controls. Compare lawful acquisition cohorts using settled fees, and price jurisdictional restrictions into the reachable traffic pool.

The mapped play telecom_voice_traffic_pumping_8yy_sms_arbitrage requires a hard distinction between genuine customer utility and artificial traffic designed to extract intercarrier payments. FCC access-stimulation restrictions and tariff obligations, including relevant provisions of 47 CFR Part 61, constrain covered arrangements; Part 61 is not a complete account of every 8YY or messaging rule. Do not budget profit from fabricated calls, induced routing loops, or inflated billable minutes. A legitimate model can charge for useful inbound call handling, appointment routing, or opt-in SMS service with clear customer value and permitted carrier use. Measure completed service interactions, customer retention, carrier charges, and complaint rates rather than raw traffic volume. Opt-in alone does not resolve every messaging requirement. Verify the applicable consent, identification, opt-out, carrier, and numbering rules for the actual service before treating a telecom partner's payout schedule as durable revenue.

The mapped play agency_ad_spend_card_multiplier_rebate_cycling is a cost adjustment, not a second profit engine. Model eligible realized card points or rebates as a two to four percent media-cost reduction only when issuer commercial-card terms, reward caps, redemption values, and payment discipline support it. At $100,000 eligible spend, that is $2,000 to $4,000 before interest, fees, or lost discounts; debt costs can erase the benefit. Exclude manufactured spend, circular transactions, and client funds whose reward ownership is unresolved. Record a qualifying purchase rebate against the related cost in this management model, with the accountant determining tax treatment from the actual arrangement. Section 162 supports ordinary and necessary business expense deductions but does not classify every reward. Separately, Part 255 calls for clear disclosure of material affiliate relationships; truthful offer comparisons protect conversion quality as well as the reader.

callout.title: Reject revenue that depends on invalid activity
callout.body: An attractive EPC cannot rescue prohibited acquisition, artificial telecom demand, or rewards unsupported by issuer terms. These checks concern the specific mapped plays, not extra software interfaces.
items: Document state-specific gaming affiliate status and negative-carryover terms.
Reject promo abuse and reconcile every scrub reason.
Require real telecom utility and permitted carrier arrangements.
Value rewards only after caps, fees, and contractual ownership.
Place material-relationship disclosures with the endorsement.

sections.heading: 5. Reconcile the annual model before buying growth
paragraphs: Candidate #24's annual scenarios start with gross earned commissions net of reversals: $50,000 conservative, $325,000 base, and $600,000 scaled. Here gross means before operating expenses, not before scrubs. Their exact owner profit targets are $10,000 at twenty percent margin, $113,750 at thirty-five percent, and $300,000 at fifty percent. Staffing is 1 FT + 2 C in both conservative and base, then 2 FT + 3 C at scale; FT denotes full-time capacity and C denotes contractors. In this model the owner supplies one FT role and receives the residual profit rather than a salary charged again as an expense. People costs cover nonowner labor and limited contractor hours. This is a workload assumption, not a claim that the conservative budget buys three market-rate salaries. Price a replacement owner salary separately when assessing whether the operation is an attractive investment rather than merely a job.

The annual table is a complete illustrative operating profit bridge, not an extrapolation of the monthly paid cohort. Its different margins require different traffic mixes, operating costs, and mature recurring stacks. Media is shown net of any realized qualifying rebates; never subtract those rewards again below profit. Content includes production work outside the people line, tools include software and tracking, and other costs include finance charges and remaining overhead. Actual employer taxes and contractor fees belong in people costs where incurred. Owner profit is before owner income taxes and distributions. No merchant GMV is included and no reversal reserve is deducted twice. A business with equipment purchases, debt principal, or rising receivables also needs a cash-flow bridge because those items change cash without matching this profit statement. Replace each assumption with booked actuals monthly and explain the variance before adopting a higher revenue target.

Use milestones that test the mechanism instead of treating an annual target as a spend instruction. During the first week, capture the current offer terms and rebuild the click-to-settlement ledger for existing cohorts. During the second, calculate reversal-adjusted EPC and retained subscription value using only observed data, with explicit ranges where evidence is thin. During the third, map weekly cash needs through the longest applicable lock and settlement schedule and price committed financing. During the fourth, authorize only the incremental spend that the downside model can fund while preserving its buffer. These weeks establish measurement, not proof that a ninety day cohort has matured. Keep tracking beyond the first month until cash arrives and late reversals are understood. Move toward the scaled case only when repeatable acquisition, retained commissions, and staffing capacity explain the improvement in margin; a larger credit limit alone explains none of it.

chapters.subtitle: $5,000-$50,000 Launch Tranches, $1,500-$12,000 Monthly Opex, Serverless Edge Comparison Hubs & Clean Expired Domain/RSS Due Diligence
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #24 earns commissions, not the merchant's checkout revenue. Build its startup budget around that distinction. A $5,000 launch buys one organic comparison wedge; $20,000 funds a hybrid co-registration and paid search bridge; $50,000 supports a bounded multi-vertical call and media test desk. None buys automatic distribution. Release cash against reconciled events, accepted calls, and mature commissions rather than traffic screenshots. Keep hosting replaceable, click identifiers durable, and acquired domains or feeds subject to documented rights review. This chapter turns the 92/100, rank #02 opportunity and its 35 mapped operator plays into a staged infrastructure purchasing plan.

sections.heading: 1. Buy evidence in three capital tranches
paragraphs: Treat startup capital as a loss ceiling, not a shopping allowance. The $5,000 organic comparison and calculator wedge starts with one buyer problem, one merchant shortlist, and a useful calculator whose assumptions readers can inspect. The $20,000 hybrid co-registration and paid search bridge testbed adds a named partner, explicit lead permissions, and tightly capped search cohorts. The $50,000 multi-vertical pay-per-call and media-arbitrage desk adds routing, buyer schedules, and separate ledgers for each vertical. These are alternative starting designs, not three mandatory stages. Do not buy an expired asset merely because its auction ends tonight. Reserve money for disputed commissions, broken integrations, and the weeks between traffic purchase and merchant settlement. A tranche is successful when it answers a commercial question cheaply enough to leave cash for the next test, not when every allocated dollar has been spent.

Use the allocation table as a cash deployment map rather than an accounting classification. Content includes original comparisons, calculator inputs, and merchant fact checking. Infrastructure includes implementation as well as initial service charges; media means a finite test budget rather than an evergreen commitment. The reserve remains unspent until a dated decision releases it. Budget the $1,500-$12,000 monthly operating envelope separately, then identify which launch invoices already cover the first month's services so they are not counted twice. At the low end, the founder supplies most editorial and engineering labor; a full market salary would require additional capital. At the upper end, acquisition bursts can exceed the stated envelope and must have their own funded ceiling. A cheap hosting bill does not make a staffed affiliate operation cheap, especially when buyers pay after the traffic supplier has collected.

Separate cash survival from tax treatment before authorizing purchases. Section 195 generally prevents an immediate deduction for startup expenditures except through its election framework: up to $5,000 may be deducted, reduced by startup costs above $50,000, with the remaining qualifying amount amortized over 180 months beginning when the active business starts. These thresholds apply to qualifying startup expenditures, not automatically to the entire launch tranche. Acquired assets, software development, and ongoing operating bills may require different treatment. Record invoice purpose, service period, business commencement date, and the basis for classification. Do not call a reserve a deductible expense merely because it appears in a budget. Keep a cash ledger for survival decisions and a classification schedule for the tax preparer. Tax timing can change reported income without producing the settlement cash needed to keep campaigns running next week.

sections.heading: 2. Make the comparison hub cheap to idle and easy to leave
paragraphs: Implement serverless_edge_free_tier_empire_hosting as a static publishing discipline, not a promise of unlimited free compute. Export Astro or supported static Next pages to Cloudflare Pages, with Workers handling the small dynamic redirect surface. Precompute comparison tables and calculator reference data; keep merchant API calls out of the reader's critical rendering path. Aim for <100ms warm edge time to first byte in selected target regions, then report the measured percentile and cache state. That target is not total page load time and cannot be assumed for every visitor. Test cold requests, mobile networks, and geographic misses separately. Keep images compressed and scripts optional where possible. The calculator should still explain its inputs if JavaScript fails. Publish a dated methodology beside numerical outputs so speed never becomes a substitute for defensible comparisons or current merchant terms in a changing offer market.

Use server-side click-ID injection on an owned outbound route rather than caching personalized identifiers inside public HTML. When a visitor follows a merchant link, the Worker creates a random opaque identifier, records the permitted source fields, and appends the identifier using the merchant's supported sub-ID parameter. Never place an email address or telephone number in the URL. Mark the redirect response non-cacheable, allowlist destinations, and validate parameter length and encoding. Store timestamps in UTC and retain the offer version that was shown. If event storage is unavailable, either use a documented untracked direct link or suspend paid acquisition; do not silently report that click as attributed. Repeated reloads must not create fictitious conversions. A later server-to-server callback links the merchant transaction to the original click without requiring a browser pixel to survive every subsequent page visit or device setting.

Zero-idle describes architecture that avoids paying for an always-running application server; it does not erase domains, monitoring, databases, call numbers, or usage charges. Keep the source, static export, DNS inventory, redirect rules, and event schema under your control. Schedule exports to portable storage and restore a sample before traffic becomes expensive. Review free-tier quotas against actual request volume and bot load, not just human sessions. Set an alert before paid overages become material and restrict abusive requests without blocking merchant callbacks. Use a separate callback endpoint with authentication and bounded retries. During an outage, serve a versioned static comparison page and make any unavailable calculator state explicit. A backup that preserves pages but loses click mappings protects appearance rather than economics. Assign one person to test both content restoration and transaction reconciliation monthly, with a dated record of the outcome.

callout.title: Edge Hosting, Cloaked-Route & Expired-Domain Secrets
callout.body: Technical super-affiliates eliminate attribution leakage and auction traps with four infrastructure habits:
items: Never Expose Raw Affiliate Network Domains in Page HTML: Route every CTA through first-party `/go/offer-slug` Edge Worker endpoints (`302` + `Cache-Control: no-store`) so ad-block lists never strip buttons and swapping a paused merchant updates 50 pages in 5 seconds.

Avoid Third-Party Link-Shortener SaaS Lock-In: Hosted link shorteners break ad-account destination-mismatch rules when domain roots differ; always run tracking & redirects on a first-party path or CNAME of your comparison domain.

Run the '5-Year Wayback Language & Casino Check' Before Any Drop-Catch Bid: Over 60% of high-DR auction domains were briefly repurposed for Chinese/Russian pharma or PBN gambling links—if Wayback shows a single off-topic language pivot, walk away.

Pre-Render Comparison Pricing Tables as Static HTML, Never Client-Only React State: Both Googlebot and LLM RAG crawlers (Perplexity/ChatGPT Search) index static `<table>` cells reliably while frequently dropping client-hydrated pricing tabs.

sections.heading: 3. Connect twelve layers without losing the transaction
paragraphs: The reference matrix prices a planning configuration, not a verified vendor tariff. Launch allowances total $160 monthly; scale allowances total $2,960 before traffic, content, labor, taxes, and variable call overages. Several tools can share one account, so remove duplicated charges when obtaining quotes. The lower stack budget leaves roughly $1,340 inside a $1,500 operating month for limited contractor work and maintenance, with founder time supplied separately. A $12,000 month could allocate $2,960 to infrastructure, $3,000 to content and operations, $5,000 to controlled acquisition, and $1,040 to other recurring costs. These examples are spending envelopes, not forecasts of profitable demand. A call-heavy vertical may consume the telephony allowance before generating enough accepted calls. Monitor cost per accepted call alongside minutes and numbers, because cheap raw calls can become expensive rejected inventory once the buyer applies qualification rules.

Design one transaction ledger before choosing a tracker interface. Store click ID, partner, offer version, event ID, merchant transaction ID, event time, currency, commission amount, and status. Authenticate callbacks using the partner's supported signature or shared secret, and protect secrets outside page code. Deduplicate using partner plus event ID, while allowing legitimate status changes for the same transaction. A refund is a reversal entry, not a deletion of inconvenient history. Queue transient failures, cap retry attempts, and retain a repair queue for manual reconciliation. Compare merchant statements with the ledger at least weekly and again at settlement. A tracker can prove what it received, not what the merchant never sent. Maintain discrepancy counts by partner so a missing callback does not masquerade as low conversion or cause you to abandon an otherwise sound traffic cohort prematurely.

Call routing adds inventory constraints that page analytics cannot see. Record buyer hours, timezone, capacity, geographic coverage, qualification criteria, and rejection reasons before opening a campaign. Distinguish a dial, a connected call, a qualified call, an accepted payable call, and cash received. Route overflow only to buyers authorized for that source and purpose; otherwise stop spending or provide an honest unavailable state. For co-registration, retain the exact permission language and recipient scope associated with each submitted lead. Never treat purchased contact data as transferable permission. If recording is enabled, determine applicable requirements and configure the required disclosures and permissions; recording is not essential to every routing design. Keep raw personal data out of general analytics exports. The useful weekly report joins campaign spend to accepted outcomes and eventual settlement rather than celebrating call duration as if every minute created revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Acquire rights and useful audiences, not inherited liabilities
paragraphs: Run domain_drop_catch_backlink_parking_arbitrage as documented asset diligence rather than a shortcut to another business's reputation. Screen generic expiring names for trademark conflicts, including confusing similarity and the intended use, before assigning any backlink value. A dictionary word is not automatically safe in every commercial context. The ACPA in 15 U.S.C. section 1125(d) addresses specified domain conduct involving bad-faith intent to profit from protected marks; evaluate the statutory factors rather than assuming expiration extinguishes earlier rights. Inspect archived pages across multiple years, anchor text, referring domains, language changes, and sudden ownership pivots. Look for hacked pharmaceutical pages, doorway networks, and unrelated outbound links. A clean current screenshot cannot erase a polluted history. Value the name first as a usable address, then discount speculative traffic severely. Do not pay for a seller's claim that historical rankings will transfer unchanged to a different business.

Apply expired_podcast_rss_redirect_arbitrage only to consented, unencumbered retired feeds or domains with a documented chain of authority. Domain control alone does not transfer episode copyright, host identity, artwork, music licenses, subscriber data, or the right to impersonate the former show. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a transfer of copyright ownership generally requires a writing signed by the owner or authorized agent, except transfers by operation of law. Inventory each asset and its separate rights; a feed may contain licensed material the seller cannot assign. Obtain the retiring owner's authorization for any transition and verify platform migration requirements. Introduce the new publisher honestly instead of silently replacing a trusted voice with affiliate advertisements. If rights are incomplete, buy only the clearly transferable asset or walk away. Listener counts are not evidence that listeners agreed to receive unrelated commercial material from a successor.

Put diligence findings into the valuation model before negotiating price. Estimate useful visits after removing bots, irrelevant geography, branded navigational searches, and traffic dependent on content you cannot lawfully reuse. Demand dated analytics evidence and reconcile it against server logs where available, with personal data minimized. For feeds, distinguish downloads from reachable, interested listeners and avoid forecasting revenue from old subscriber totals. Set a maximum acquisition price from a conservative incremental contribution estimate after migration costs, content replacement, and ongoing maintenance. Assign zero value to traffic that requires confusion or unauthorized reuse to monetize. Keep an evidence packet containing archive samples, ownership documents, transfer scope, restrictions, and planned redirects. If the packet is incomplete, reduce the bid or leave the auction. The durable fallback is a new generic domain with original content, not increasingly elaborate explanations for a questionable asset purchase.

sections.heading: 5. Underwrite owner profit with mature cohorts and cash milestones
paragraphs: Candidate #24 uses gross earned commissions to mean affiliate revenue after reversals but before operating expenses. Referred merchant gross merchandise value is a separate volume measure and never enters the affiliate revenue line. For a worked annual base illustration, suppose attributed merchant GMV is $3,500,000 and the contractual commission rate is 10%. That produces $350,000 before $25,000 of reversals and clawbacks, leaving $325,000 gross earned commissions. Subtract $211,250 of total operating costs to reach $113,750 owner net profit, a 35% margin. The rate and reversal amount are illustrative assumptions, not universal merchant terms. Track approved, payable, and paid amounts separately because earned commissions can remain unpaid at year end. Owner profit here means residual operating profit before owner income tax, debt service, and distributions, with the modeled staffing cost included and no additional founder salary silently assumed elsewhere in the calculation.

The three annual scenarios are economic targets, not a claim that the launch opex envelope can support every scale. Conservative commissions of $50,000 less $40,000 costs leave $10,000 at 20% margin with 1 FT + 2 C. Base commissions of $325,000 less $211,250 costs leave $113,750 at 35% with 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled commissions of $600,000 less $300,000 costs leave $300,000 at 50% with 2 FT + 3 C. FT denotes full-time roles and C denotes contractors, not equal salaries or guaranteed employment capacity. The conservative design assumes the founder fills the full-time role and contractors work limited hours; a paid replacement could consume the residual profit. Base and scaled monthly average costs exceed $12,000, so expansion requires additional acquisition and labor funding rather than pretending the startup envelope remains the complete operating budget indefinitely.

Release the next traffic tranche only after a cohort has passed the merchant's relevant reversal window and reconciles to a statement. For a paid-search test, assume 1,000 clicks cost $2,000, create ten initial conversions at $400 commission, and lose one conversion to reversal. Earned commissions are $3,600; after traffic and $600 allocated content, tooling, and labor, contribution is $1,000 before any remaining shared overhead. Break-even earned conversion rate under these assumptions is 0.65%, versus the observed 0.9%; neither rate predicts the next cohort. Segment by offer and source so one profitable campaign does not conceal another's losses. During the first week, finish the calculator and synthetic event tests. During weeks two and three, buy a capped cohort. After settlement, compare cash received with costs already paid, refresh the reserve forecast, and expand only the sources whose reconciled economics justify the additional exposure.

chapters.question_prompt: What do experienced super-affiliates know that beginners miss?
chapters.title: What Experienced Super-Affiliates Know That Beginners Miss
chapters.subtitle: Surviving Google Site Reputation Abuse Enforcement, Preventing Last-Click Coupon Poaching, Authorized Brand-Bidding Rights & First-Party Lead Ownership
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #24 ranks #02 with 92/100 and 35 mapped operator plays. Its durable edge is control over distribution, contract rights, attribution evidence, and audience access. This chapter turns three fragile plays into defensible operating systems without confusing merchant sales with affiliate income. Search visibility can disappear; merchants can cut rates; checkout tools can overwrite credit. Build around earned commissions after reversals, then subtract every operating cost before calling the remainder profit. Use the defense matrix, attribution procedure, audience experiment, and scenario ledger to decide which traffic deserves another dollar and which exposure needs replacing.

sections.heading: 1. Own the recommendation, not borrowed search rank
paragraphs: The parasitic_seo play mistakes rented authority for an owned sales channel. An unedited affiliate subfolder on a strong publisher domain may rank before its operator has earned any trust. That does not make the traffic durable. Google's Site Reputation Abuse policy targets third party content placed to exploit a host site's ranking signals; editorial involvement alone does not make that arrangement safe. A loss of visibility can arrive before the next payroll cycle, although no precise enforcement date is predictable. Replace the rent seeking premise with original tests, named reviewers, useful comparisons, and distribution that does not depend on the host. The merchant should still receive qualified buyers if the publisher stops ranking tomorrow. Treat overnight disappearance as a stress case, not a forecast or a claim that every guest contribution violates policy.

Before buying a placement, ask who owns the page, who can change its claims, and who keeps the audience when the agreement ends. Review actual products rather than recycling merchant copy. Save the evidence behind each comparison and date every price statement. A publisher can legitimately sell advertising, but paid access to ranking signals is not a permanent business asset. Separate referral visits from search visits in reporting, and require a clear sponsorship disclosure where the relationship would affect how readers weigh a recommendation. A page with no independent reader value is not rescued by adding a staff biography. Make the test concrete: would a buyer bookmark this page if search engines never sent another visitor? If not, spend the next production cycle building something worth returning to instead of renewing the placement.

Measure search dependence at the profit level, not just the traffic level. A channel that supplies half the visits may supply nearly all profitable sales. Keep a weekly register of earned commissions by page, host, merchant, and acquisition source, allowing for the settlement delay. Model losing the largest host while retaining fixed costs for the next eight weeks. If cash runs out, cut commitments before increasing production. Export your original work under the rights you actually hold and maintain an independent destination for returning readers. Do not move the same abusive arrangement to another publisher and call that diversification. The durable replacement is a useful recommendation business with multiple routes to its audience, not a portfolio of hosts exposed to the same policy and the same sudden loss of search demand.

sections.heading: 2. Price merchant dependence before buying growth
paragraphs: Suppose one merchant provides eighty percent of earned commissions and cuts its rate from thirty percent to five percent overnight. Hold eligible sales volume and reversal rates constant to isolate the shock. That merchant now pays one sixth of its former amount; the remaining portfolio keeps its old earnings. Total commissions fall to one third of the starting level, a loss of roughly two thirds before any cost savings. This is not an eighty percent traffic problem. It is a contract pricing problem that can destroy a profitable acquisition budget while traffic looks healthy. Read notice periods, exclusions, and amendment rights before accepting the exposure. Record the effective date and which transactions receive the old rate. Never assume an announced rate change applies retroactively or that pending earnings are protected without checking the agreement.

Build substitutes while the leading offer still works. Compare customer fit, eligible order value, refund patterns, payout timing, support quality, and the merchant's ability to close qualified leads. A nominally higher rate can produce less cash if the sales team misses calls or the program rejects renewals. Send a limited matched cohort to a second merchant and wait through its reversal window before declaring victory. Keep a route for customers whose needs the first merchant cannot meet rather than forcing every reader into the same offer. Set a concentration ceiling from the cash loss you can withstand, not from a universal percentage borrowed from another business. The useful question is whether the company survives losing its largest contribution stream while still paying staff and honoring its existing production commitments through the replacement period.

Keep three amounts separate in every review: referred merchant gross merchandise value, affiliate commissions earned after reversals, and owner net profit after operating costs. A million dollars of customer purchases is not a million dollars of publisher revenue. Pending commissions are not settled cash either. Track the difference between booked, approved, payable, and received amounts, with the merchant's reason codes attached to changes. A contract may permit unpaid balance forfeiture for prohibited promotion; do not describe that outcome as automatic under every program or as a statutory penalty. Ask for the specific clause, an evidence trail, and a dispute route. Budget traffic, content, tooling, staff, and contractors against collectible commission income. When evidence is missing, preserve the disputed amount separately rather than making payroll depend on an optimistic dashboard number that the merchant has not accepted.

callout.title: Super-Affiliate Defenses Against Poaching & Rate Cuts
callout.body: Seven-figure referral operators insulate their margins from platform and merchant shocks with four structural plays:
items: Request a Dedicated Vanity Partner Code Alongside Your S2S Link: When a buyer watches your YouTube teardown on mobile and types the URL on desktop later, an exclusive 10%-off or extended-trial partner code (`SWITCHLAB`) captures cross-device conversions cookies miss.

Audit 'BrandVerity / AdPolice' Broad-Match Leaks Weekly: Even honest non-brand Google Ads (`best payroll software`) match `[merchant name] payroll` under Broad Match unless every restricted partner brand is locked in an account-level Phrase/Exact negative list.

Negotiate 30-Day Written Rate-Protection Windows: Standard network clickwrap lets merchants cut payouts on 24 hours' notice; once you deliver 15+ monthly customers, ask for a 30-day written rate-change notice rider so paid media never gets ambushed mid-flight.

Keep Runner-Up Offer 'Warm' With 15%-20% Split Traffic: Never wait until Offer A pauses or slashes commissions to apply to Offer B—send 15%-20% of calculator traffic to Offer B continuously so your S2S postback, AM relationship, and VIP tier stay hot.

sections.heading: 3. Replace stolen intent with explicit commercial rights
paragraphs: The mapped play typo_squatting_brand_bid_hijacking belongs in the replacement ledger, not the launch queue. Do not register confusing typo domains or run covert geo-cloaked brand ads to escape merchant review. The ACPA addresses qualifying domain conduct involving bad faith intent to profit; trademark advertising raises separate confusion and representation questions under section 1125(a). Nominative fair use depends on facts and jurisdiction, not on an affiliate's declaration. Replace these tactics with written merchant TM+ co-bidding addenda or truthful [Competitor] vs [Brand] comparison ads that satisfy platform rules and relevant rights. A merchant's permission cannot license a competitor's mark or override law. The addendum should identify allowed queries, territories, ad language, destinations, exclusions, bidding limits, and termination treatment. Without those particulars, a friendly email saying to drive more volume is weak protection against a later unpaid balance dispute.

The mapped play coupon_checkout_tab_under_injection requires an equally decisive replacement. Banned tab-under tools and forced cookie-stuffing injectors can assign affiliate credit without a deliberate customer referral. They expose balances to program sanctions and erase the distinction between generating demand and taking credit for an existing buyer. Use transparent merchant-authorized promo or cashback pages instead, with verified terms and an intentional outbound action. Test code eligibility, expiry, minimum spend, product exclusions, and cashback payment timing before publication. Do not promise that a code works merely because it attracts searches. Put the commercial relationship where buyers encounter the recommendation, consistent with the FTC endorsement guides. A disclosure buried in a footer cannot reliably explain a paid recommendation several screens away. Measure whether the page helps a buyer choose or save, rather than celebrating every last click as newly created demand.

Last-click coupon poaching is an attribution diagnosis, not a label for every coupon publisher. A buyer may discover your review, reach checkout, search for a code, and legitimately click another affiliate under the merchant's attribution rules. Preserve permitted referral identifiers, timestamps, campaign tags, and settlement records to distinguish that sequence from a forced overwrite. Request merchant-side evidence without collecting unnecessary customer details. Negotiate attribution windows, protected lead rules, or split credit where the program supports them; do not assume any particular model is available. An owned audience can give you another chance to help the buyer, but it does not confer ownership of the sale. Compare capture against direct linking with matched traffic and settled economics. The table sets a bounded experiment whose assumptions can be challenged, rather than presenting capture as an automatic increase in profit.

sections.heading: 4. Capture a useful relationship before surrendering the visit
paragraphs: Sending cold traffic straight to a merchant homepage combines two weaknesses: the destination may not answer the buyer's question, and you lose the ability to help if they leave. Offer a useful first party asset before the referral: an email buying guide, an optional SMS reminder, or a quiz that produces a genuine recommendation. Keep an accessible route for visitors who prefer to continue without subscribing. Ownership here means control over a permissioned relationship and portable records, not unrestricted rights over a person or their data. Explain the follow-up they will receive, separate email from SMS choices, and honor withdrawal. Collect only what improves the recommendation. A quiz about business software needs workflow and budget information, not sensitive personal history. Match the outbound destination to the identified use case instead of dropping every visitor onto the merchant's generic homepage.

The capture comparison assumes identical traffic quality and a fixed thirty day measurement window. Direct linking produces ten orders; capture produces fifteen orders from two hundred fifty leads, including any immediate purchases within that group. Count each order once. Both routes pay the same acquisition bill, use the same order value, and suffer the same modeled reversal rate. Capture adds two hundred dollars of messaging and infrastructure cost. Its eleven hundred dollar contribution exceeds direct linking by seven hundred dollars, but the conclusion reverses if lead quality or follow-up conversion deteriorates enough. At one hundred eighty dollars of earned commission per order, capture needs more than eleven orders to beat the direct route's four hundred dollar contribution under these assumptions. Round to twelve orders for an operational target, then verify settlement rather than extrapolating from form submissions.

Run the experiment with a stable allocation rule and preserve channel, device, and offer mixes across groups. Compare outcomes only after both cohorts have had equal time to buy and reverse. Track delivery failures, unsubscribes, sales, and earned commissions per original visitor; a higher capture rate alone proves little. Keep the recommendation useful even when the best product pays nothing, because credibility supports future visits. Export permission records and source tags regularly so a messaging vendor outage does not erase the relationship. Stop follow-up when someone withdraws permission, and do not treat email permission as permission to text. Budget the labor required to maintain the sequence and answer replies. The owned asset is economically real only when it produces incremental collectible income after those costs, not when a database contains a large number of unreachable or uninterested contacts.

callout.title: Spend follows rights and settled evidence
callout.body: Expand only the tactic whose permissions, attribution, and cash contribution can be demonstrated. A failed check stops that tactic, not the whole business.
items: Brand campaigns match the written TM+ addendum and platform rules.
Promo referrals require an intentional customer action; no forced overwrites.
Email and SMS records support the actual follow-up channel used.
Matched cohorts outperform after reversals and incremental operating costs.

sections.heading: 5. Underwrite the business on retained commissions
paragraphs: Candidate #24's three scenarios are annual planning cases, not reported operator outcomes. Gross earned commissions means affiliate revenue after reversals and clawbacks but before operating expenses; it never means referred merchant GMV. The ledger uses a twenty percent nominal commission rate and ten percent reversal rate solely to bridge merchant volume to the specified earned revenue. Actual programs require their own rates, exclusions, and refund history. Divide earned commissions by eighteen percent to obtain the illustrative eligible GMV. Then subtract traffic, content, tooling, labor, and other operating expenses to reach owner net profit. These profit figures are before the owner's personal income tax and exclude financing effects. Count compensation for work once in the cost envelope; residual profit is not another salary expense. The distinction prevents a sales volume headline from hiding a weak publisher business.

Conservative operations retain fifty thousand dollars of commissions and spend forty thousand dollars, leaving ten thousand dollars at a twenty percent margin. The base case retains three hundred twenty five thousand dollars and spends two hundred eleven thousand two hundred fifty dollars, leaving one hundred thirteen thousand seven hundred fifty dollars at thirty five percent. Scaled operations retain six hundred thousand dollars and spend three hundred thousand dollars, leaving three hundred thousand dollars at fifty percent. These are the required planning identities, not proof that the staffing is affordable. One full time operator plus two contractors must fit the conservative and base envelopes; two full time operators plus three contractors must fit the scaled envelope. Contractor counts say nothing about hours. If realistic compensation exceeds the envelope, the scenario fails and needs higher commissions or a different cost structure.

Use milestones tied to evidence rather than celebrating a larger dashboard balance. In the first week, reconcile the largest merchant and document channel rights. During the next three weeks, launch a small substitute offer test and the matched capture experiment. After a complete settlement cycle, update costs and reversal assumptions from actual cohorts before expanding spend. The concentration shock shown below holds noncommission costs constant and assumes the exposed merchant represents eighty percent of earned revenue in each case. That deliberately harsh test makes the downside visible without pretending to estimate its probability. Maintain a separate cash calendar for payout delays and disputed balances; accounting profit cannot pay bills before collection. Scale only when replacement distribution, verified attribution, and sufficient liquidity survive the modeled loss. A bigger affiliate operation should become harder to break, not merely more expensive to stop.

chapters.question_prompt: How do I find winning offers and buyers ready to act?
chapters.title: Finding Your First Winning Offers & Bottom-of-Funnel Buyer Intent
chapters.subtitle: Ad-Library Spend-Velocity Mining, "[Incumbent] Pricing / Cancel / Alternative" Query Interception, Programmatic XML Job Feeds & Private CPA Bump Scripts
chapters.executive_summary: Buy evidence of intent, not cheap visits. Candidate #24 ranks #02 with 92/100 and 35 mapped operator plays; this chapter turns three plays into a repeatable offer test. Start with pricing, comparison, migration, and verified hiring queries. Use persistent ads to select experiments, never to infer profit. Secure written traffic terms, publish useful comparison pages, and reconcile clicks to accepted commissions after reversals. A seven day test can reject bad economics; it cannot prove lifetime performance. Negotiate a private payout increase only with documented lead quality. Keep merchant sales, affiliate earnings, operating costs, and owner profit in separate ledger columns.

sections.heading: 1. Qualify intent before buying a click
paragraphs: Start with the buyer's next costly decision, not a topic with a large search count. A reader asking what CRM means may be months from a purchase; a team asking for a pricing calculator needs a bill they can defend this week. Treat the $0.05 EPC for broad informational visits as an illustrative warning, not a universal rate. EPC here means earned affiliate commissions after reversals divided by tracked outbound affiliate clicks. Paid search uses a different denominator: purchased visits to your page. Record both counts so a high outbound EPC cannot hide a page that sends almost no visitors to the merchant. Build a short list of offers around one buyer task, one geography, and one purchase window. Then check whether each program pays for a lead, a trial, an accepted application, or a completed sale before comparing payouts.

Make qualification mechanical enough that a contractor can repeat it without inventing demand. For each query, record the implied purchase, the obstacle preventing action, the page needed to remove that obstacle, and the program that can legitimately fulfill it. A comparison deserves measured differences; a migration deserves an export checklist, implementation effort, and known limitations. Cancellation deserves the actual cancellation instructions before any alternative recommendation. Use the twelve signals as evidence categories rather than a magical weighted score. Several signals may describe the same underlying demand and should not be counted as independent confirmations. Reject an offer when its geography, audience restrictions, or payable event does not match the query. Save the rejection reason. That small discipline prevents a later researcher from reviving a large advertised payout whose terms make your intended traffic worthless in practice.

Model six to sixteen percent click to lead or trial as an experiment range for commercial investigation traffic, not a forecast inherited from the category. Define the click as an outbound affiliate click before comparing cohorts. At one hundred outbound clicks, that range implies six to sixteen submissions, not six to sixteen commissions. Approval, activation, purchase, and retention may still intervene. Track a separate bridge page outbound rate so the purchased visit economics remain visible. The best starting query is therefore not necessarily the one with the highest response rate: it is the one with affordable acquisition, a relevant offer, an observable payable event, and tolerable reversal exposure. Choose two tightly related query clusters for the first test. Keep device, geography, and landing page consistent enough that a difference in results can guide a real operating decision.

sections.heading: 2. Mine activity, then build a useful destination
paragraphs: The play ad_library_spend_velocity_arbitrage is a research filter, not access to a competitor's bank account. Keep a dated log of ads found in Meta, Google Ads Transparency Center, and TikTok Creative Center. Track advertiser identity, first observed date, last observed date, offer wording, creative changes, destination, and region. Repeated observations spanning at least thirty days support an activity hypothesis. They do not establish continuous delivery, actual spend velocity, accepted lead quality, or profit. Some libraries expose only selected material, and absence is not proof that an advertiser stopped spending. Rank patterns by persistence and relevance to your chosen buyer task, then test your own unit EPC. A strong incumbent may have better retention, private payouts, or direct sales economics that you cannot copy. Borrow the research question, not their creative, customer claims, identity, or assumed cost structure.

The play competitor_intent_comparison_hijacking means earning attention with a better answer, not impersonating an incumbent. Build a dated calculator for [Software] pricing calculator, a substantiated [Vendor] vs [Vendor] comparison, or a practical guide for how to switch from [Incumbent]. Show seat counts, currency, billing cycle, mandatory fees, and the date each price was checked. Distinguish published terms from estimates and link the underlying merchant pages. Explain migration limitations instead of implying every workflow transfers automatically. Use competitor names only as needed to identify the comparison, avoid confusing branding, and never imply sponsorship. Nominative fair use is context dependent, not an automatic shield; section 1125(a) addresses false association and misleading representations. Put a clear affiliate relationship disclosure near the recommendation, consistent with the endorsement guides, rather than hiding the financial connection in a remote page footer.

For job_board_xml_feed_programmatic_arbitrage, start with legitimate employer feeds and explicit republication rights. Preserve employer identifiers and stable job IDs; enrich salary, location, shift, licensing, and bonus eligibility only from reliable authorized data. A CDL sign on bonus may require a specific license class, driving history, and repayment commitment. A travel nurse bonus may depend on specialty, contract duration, start date, and completed hours. State those conditions without turning maximum possible compensation into a universal salary promise. Refresh on the employer's schedule, display verification dates, deduplicate listings, and remove closed jobs promptly. If a feed fails, suspend uncertain inventory rather than silently treating yesterday's vacancy as live. Unique useful context can improve the application experience; thousands of thin pages cannot repair inaccurate inventory. Section 45 makes deceptive commercial claims relevant to this model even when the misleading data originated upstream.

callout.title: BOFU Query Mining & Private Payout-Bump Secrets
callout.body: Top B2B affiliates win approvals and private rate tiers faster by reversing how beginners approach partner managers:
items: Ship One Working Comparison Calculator BEFORE Applying to Tier-1 Programs: Enterprise SaaS managers reject 80% of blank 'I run SEO/ads' applications; applying with a live, fast, FTC-disclosed calculator URL wins instant approval and Slack access.

Target 'Zero-Volume' High-ACV Integration Queries (`[CRM] + [ERP] sync cost`): Keyword tools report '0-10/mo' on B2B integration queries where 8 monthly clicks yield two $1,000 closed-won deals—mine Google Search Console & sales-call FAQs instead.

Ask for a '30-Day Volume-Tier Step-Up' Instead of an Unconditional Bump: Managers rarely grant a blind +30% CPA hike on Day 1, but routinely sign 'Default $500 CPA; steps retroactively to $650 CPA in any calendar month with >=10 qualified demos.'

Mystery-Shop the Merchant's Demo Funnel Before Spending Paid Dollars: Book a disclosed test walkthrough or inspect their calendar—if the merchant's form errors on mobile or offers no AE slots for 9 days, your EPC will crater regardless of payout size.

sections.heading: 3. Secure terms and negotiate from accepted cohorts
paragraphs: An affiliate manager needs a distribution plan they can evaluate, not a promise of unlimited traffic. Send the exact page concept, intended search themes, audience location, acquisition channel, and a sample disclosure. Ask whether paid search, competitor keywords, brand bidding, bridge pages, and recruiting traffic are permitted separately; permission for one does not establish permission for another. Request the payable event definition, attribution window, duplicate rules, existing customer exclusions, reversal reasons, reporting delay, and payment schedule. Save the written answer beside the offer record. A recruiting offer may require a completed qualified application rather than a form submission, while software may pay only after a trial becomes a paying account. Compare those events before ranking commissions. If the manager cannot explain acceptance, run no financial forecast that quietly treats every submitted lead as earned revenue or available operating cash.

Use a private twenty five percent CPA increase as a negotiated change in price, not a substitute for fixing traffic quality. First reconcile a mature cohort: clicks, submitted events, accepted events, rejected events, reversals, and paid commissions. Ask the manager to confirm downstream quality without requesting personal applicant or customer records. Then propose a bounded test with a named effective date, eligible channel, volume range, and review date. Clarify whether the increase applies prospectively, retroactively, or only above a threshold. A move from $100 to $125 is a twenty five percent increase; an extra twenty five percentage points of revenue share is a different deal. Do not count the higher rate until it is confirmed in writing and appears correctly in reporting. Retain the original rate as the downside case when deciding whether additional traffic is affordable.

The outreach scripts below are templates with explicit placeholders, not invented performance evidence. Replace every bracket with a verified fact or leave the claim out. A new publisher can sell a narrow, useful execution plan without pretending to have existing volume. An established publisher should distinguish submitted leads from accepted payable events and identify the cohort's maturity date. Refusal is useful information: ask whether the constraint is quality, channel policy, economics, or capacity, then adapt only where your operation can actually improve. Never imply that a competitor has offered a higher rate unless that offer exists. Maintain a second suitable merchant so a rate negotiation does not turn your editorial recommendation into hostage bargaining. The buyer still needs the best fit for their task, even when the merchant paying the most is not that fit.

sop_steps.detail: Name pages, channels, geography, and payable event.

sop_steps.detail: Include attribution, exclusions, reversals, and payment timing.

sections.heading: 4. Run a bounded search and bridge page experiment
paragraphs: Give the first seven days a narrow job: verify tracking, measure intent, and reject obvious mismatches. They are not enough to establish mature earnings when acceptance takes weeks. Set an affordable loss limit before launch and stop purchasing traffic when that limit is reached, even if the account has not produced a statistically satisfying story. Use exact and phrase matching initially, inspect actual search terms, and exclude irrelevant research, unsupported locations, and unavailable services. Keep one main buyer action on the bridge page alongside the comparison information required to make it useful. Tag each query cluster and page version with program supported subidentifiers. Do not place personal information in tracking parameters. Compare purchased visits, outbound clicks, submitted events, and accepted events daily, preserving the cohort's original acquisition date rather than moving old conversions into today's apparent performance.

Diagnose the weakest transition before changing the payout assumption. Cheap visits with few outbound clicks usually indicate a mismatch between the query and the page's answer. Strong outbound activity with few submissions can indicate merchant friction or an unsuitable offer. Many submissions with low acceptance suggest qualification problems, duplicate users, or a misunderstood payable event. None of these diagnoses is certain from a tiny sample, so inspect the actual page and terms before declaring a cause. Pause a broken destination immediately; otherwise change one meaningful variable per new cohort. Keep a simple reconciliation sheet that separates pending amounts from earned commissions and cash received. A delayed report is not evidence of zero eventual value, but pending amounts cannot fund today's advertising bill. The operator's advantage is a disciplined feedback loop, not the willingness to keep spending until a favorable dashboard appears.

Read the scorecard as a sequence of evidence collection, not seven promises of success. On the first day, verify links and program reporting using permitted test methods; do not submit fake customer applications. During the next days, inspect query relevance, page behavior, and merchant transitions. By the seventh day, decide whether to stop, repair, or wait for acceptance data before extending spend. The table's example counts describe a single hypothetical cohort whose economics become known only after maturation. If actual acceptance remains pending, label the financial cells pending instead of filling them with the modeled numbers. Keep screenshots or exports of reporting totals with timestamps so later reversals can be reconciled. A winning first week may simply be eliminating an unsuitable offer cheaply while preserving a usable page and a clean measurement process for the next experiment.

sections.heading: 5. Translate validated demand into owner economics
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative cohort of one thousand paid search visits bought at fifty cents each. Half click through to the merchant, producing five hundred outbound affiliate clicks. Ten percent submit a lead or trial, inside the modeled six to sixteen percent range, so submissions total fifty. Suppose twenty ultimately qualify for a $100 commission, and two subsequently reverse. Earned commissions net of reversals equal $1,800, or $3.60 per outbound click and $1.80 per purchased visit. Traffic costs $500; allocated content, tooling, and labor cost another $700. The resulting $600 contribution is not automatically owner profit because unallocated overhead and financing costs may remain. Merchant GMV is neither $1,800 nor inferable from the CPA alone. Record it separately only when the merchant supplies attributable transaction value. This example demonstrates the arithmetic, not a measured campaign result or an attainable acquisition price.

A confirmed move from $100 to $125 CPA would raise the same eighteen retained payable events from $1,800 to $2,250, adding $450 before additional costs. It does not improve the page's response rate or erase rejected leads. Keep volume, acceptance, and reversals constant when isolating the payout effect; then model those assumptions separately when considering expansion. At $1,200 of cohort costs, the original eighteen events require $66.67 each to break even before any remaining overhead. A higher bid can quickly consume the negotiated benefit. Set the next cohort's budget from conservative accepted economics rather than the largest visible payout. Maintain working capital for the gap between paying for traffic and receiving commissions. A merchant can report an earned balance while withholding cash until a threshold, payment date, or review period, so the cash forecast needs its own dated schedule.

Candidate #24's annual scenarios are targets for operating design, not extrapolations from one seven day experiment. Conservative means $50,000 gross earned commissions net of reversals at twenty percent margin, leaving $10,000 owner net profit with one full time operator and two contractors. Base means $325,000 at thirty five percent, leaving $113,750 with the same staffing labels. Scaled means $600,000 at fifty percent, leaving $300,000 with two full time operators and three contractors. FT and C are staffing descriptors, not salary assumptions; the table's cost envelopes must fund actual traffic, content, tooling, labor, and overhead. State whether owner compensation and taxes are included before treating the residual as spendable income. Increase capacity only after mature cohorts support those envelopes and supplier concentration is manageable. Merchant sales volume remains separate in every scenario, regardless of how impressive the referred purchase totals look.

chapters.question_prompt: How does an affiliate build an auditable click-to-commission operating process?
chapters.title: The Complete Operating Process: Bridge Funnels, S2S Postbacks & Ping-Post
chapters.subtitle: Interactive ROI Calculators, First-Party Click-ID Ledgers, Server-to-Server (S2S) Webhook Deduplication, Ping-Post Lead Auctions & RSOC Compliance
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #24 ranks #02 with an 92/100 score and 35 mapped operator plays. Its operating advantage is not a clever redirect: it is a reconciled chain from declared intent to settled commission. Build useful bridge content, preserve first-party attribution, authenticate merchant events, and reconcile every reversal before buying more traffic. This chapter connects quiz qualification, search-feed editorial journeys, and partner web checkouts without treating them as interchangeable funnels. The annual scenarios separate merchant sales from affiliate revenue and owner profit. Instrument the chain first; scale only the traffic cohorts whose mature commissions survive refunds, scrubs, and acquisition costs.

sections.heading: 1. Build the bridge around an explicit customer decision
paragraphs: Start with the decision the visitor is trying to make, not the commission the merchant offers. An interactive ROI calculator should expose its inputs, show its arithmetic, and distinguish customer savings from affiliate earnings. Ask for current spend, transaction volume, implementation cost, and expected adoption; publish a conservative range rather than a fabricated precision score. Editorial review checks every merchant claim against dated evidence and places the material affiliate relationship beside the recommendation. Cache the static explanation at the edge and measure a sub-second initial bridge response at the ninety-fifth percentile for target geographies. That latency is an engineering target, not a promise about every device. Keep the calculator usable without third-party scripts, and measure completed decisions separately from outbound clicks so speed does not conceal poor recommendations or accidental navigation.

Treat the bridge as a small application with a documented data contract. On inbound arrival, mint an opaque random click_id and persist campaign, creative, landing version, event time, and permitted platform identifiers in a first-party ledger. Do not embed email addresses, phone numbers, or quiz answers inside the identifier. Preserve the same identifier through the calculator and send it to the merchant as sub1=click_id only where that parameter is contractually supported. If a network uses another field, map it explicitly and test the returned value. A redirect must come from an allowlisted merchant destination, never an arbitrary user-supplied URL. Failed persistence should produce a usable page without inventing attributed conversions. Record attribution availability as a separate state so missing tracking does not become a false claim that the visitor never purchased anything.

Give each release an editorial owner and an engineering owner, even when one person fills both roles. The editorial owner maintains offer eligibility, exclusions, comparison evidence, and calculator assumptions; the engineering owner maintains event schemas, redirect mappings, and reconciliation jobs. Store the published content version with the click so a disputed claim can be reconstructed later. Separate behavioral analytics from contact data, apply purpose-specific retention, and restrict exports to the minimum fields required by each destination. Monday review should compare bridge completion, merchant arrival, approved commission, and settled cash by content version. A rising outbound click rate is not success when the same cohort produces more refunds. Keep a stable comparison cohort during revisions and wait through the contractual reversal window before declaring an economically meaningful winner from an apparent conversion uplift.

rows: CREATE TABLE click_ledger (click_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, offer_slug TEXT NOT NULL, lander_ver TEXT NOT NULL, gclid TEXT, fbc TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE conversion_events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, network TEXT NOT NULL, tx_id TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, click_id TEXT, payout_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, raw_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(network, tx_id, status)); CREATE TABLE capi_outbox (event_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, network TEXT NOT NULL, tx_id TEXT NOT NULL, click_id TEXT NOT NULL, net_value_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, g_state INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, m_state INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, next_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0);
Monotone per-destination states (`0=new, 1=attempted, 2=acked, 3=reconciled_rev`), per-row `next_at` backoff, and `UNIQUE` idempotency.

const dest = ALLOWLIST[slug]; if (!dest) return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 }); const clickId = crypto.randomUUID(); const target = new URL(dest.url); try { await env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO click_ledger (click_id, offer_slug, lander_ver, gclid, fbc, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,datetime('now'))").bind(clickId, slug, ver, url.searchParams.get('gclid'), fbcCookie).run(); target.searchParams.set(dest.subParam, clickId); } catch (err) { ctx.waitUntil(logUnattributedRedirect(env, slug, err)); } return new Response(null, { status: 302, headers: { Location: target.toString(), 'Cache-Control': 'no-store, private', 'Referrer-Policy': 'strict-origin' } });
`Cache-Control: no-store` prevents shared `click_id` caching; graceful fallback redirect avoids `HTTP 500` buyer drop-off on transient D1 faults.

const raw = await request.arrayBuffer(); const sigHex = (request.headers.get('x-partner-signature') ?? '').trim(); if (!/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(sigHex)) return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 }); const sigBytes = Uint8Array.from(sigHex.match(/../g)!, b => parseInt(b, 16)); const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', new TextEncoder().encode(env.WEBHOOK_SECRET), { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['verify']); if (!(await crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', key, sigBytes, raw))) return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 });
Strict 64-hex validation + constant-time `crypto.subtle.verify` over exact raw request bytes before `JSON.parse` runs.

const eventKey = `${net}:${txId}`; const stmts = [env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO conversion_events (network, tx_id, status, click_id, payout_cents, raw_sha256, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?6,datetime('now')) ON CONFLICT(network, tx_id, status) DO NOTHING").bind(net, txId, normStatus, clickId, cents, digest)]; if (normStatus === 'approved' && clickId) { stmts.push(env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO capi_outbox (event_key, network, tx_id, click_id, net_value_cents) SELECT ?1,?2,?3,?4,?5 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversion_events WHERE network=?2 AND tx_id=?3 AND status='approved' AND raw_sha256=?6) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversion_events WHERE network=?2 AND tx_id=?3 AND status='reversed') ON CONFLICT(event_key) DO NOTHING").bind(eventKey, net, txId, clickId, Math.round(cents * 0.85), digest)); } else if (normStatus === 'reversed') { stmts.push(env.DB.prepare('UPDATE capi_outbox SET done=0, next_at=0 WHERE event_key=?1 AND (g_state < 3 OR m_state < 3)').bind(eventKey)); } const [evRes] = await env.DB.batch(stmts); ctx.waitUntil(env.OUTBOX_DO.get(env.OUTBOX_DO.idFromName('singleton')).fetch('https://do/kick')); return Response.json({ ok: true, deduped: (evRes.meta.changes ?? 0) === 0 });
`env.DB.batch` atomically commits approvals and reopens `done=0, next_at=0` on reversals while nudging the singleton `OUTBOX_DO` actor.

CREATE VIEW v_settled_tx AS SELECT network, tx_id, click_id, CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'reversed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 0 WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN status IN ('approved','paid') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN MAX(CASE WHEN status IN ('approved','paid') THEN payout_cents ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS settled_cents FROM conversion_events GROUP BY network, tx_id;
Prevents a delayed `approved` webhook retry from resurrecting a transaction that already posted `reversed`.

// wrangler.toml: [triggers] crons = ['* * * * *'] | durable_objects: OUTBOX_DO -> OutboxActor
export default { fetch, scheduled(_c: ScheduledController, env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext) { ctx.waitUntil(env.OUTBOX_DO.get(env.OUTBOX_DO.idFromName('singleton')).fetch('https://do/kick')); } }; export class OutboxActor extends DurableObject<Env> { private busy = false; private again = false; async fetch(): Promise<Response> { if (this.busy) { this.again = true; return new Response('queued'); } this.busy = true; try { do { this.again = false; await this.drain(); } while (this.again); } finally { this.busy = false; } return new Response('ok'); } private async drain() { const { results } = await this.env.DB.prepare("SELECT o.*, c.gclid, c.fbc, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM conversion_events r WHERE r.network=o.network AND r.tx_id=o.tx_id AND r.status='reversed') AS is_rev FROM capi_outbox o LEFT JOIN click_ledger c ON c.click_id=o.click_id WHERE o.done=0 AND o.next_at <= unixepoch() ORDER BY o.next_at ASC LIMIT 25").all(); sections.heading: 2. Make authenticated events reconcile to money
paragraphs: Use the ledger below as a PostgreSQL-oriented implementation skeleton, not a complete deployment. A merchant adapter must validate transaction identity, amount, currency, status vocabulary, and the original click reference before creating an event. Verify signatures over the exact raw request bytes using the partner's documented signing format; parsing and serializing first can change the signed message. A timestamp bound applies only when the partner authenticates that timestamp inside the signature input. Duplicate delivery should return success after finding the durable event, while storage failure should remain retryable. Commit event insertion and an outbound work item in one database transaction. Workers then retry uploads independently of webhook response latency. This transactional outbox prevents an acknowledged conversion from disappearing between database commit and advertising-platform submission during a worker crash or a temporary network outage.

Model commission state separately from event arrival order. A reversal can arrive before its approval, and a late approval must not resurrect a cancelled earning. Derive the current balance from validated lifecycle facts, not whichever webhook arrived last. The unique transaction and status constraint assumes one immutable amount per normalized state; partners sending partial refunds or corrected amounts need a separate adjustment ledger keyed by their adjustment identifiers. Conflicting payloads under the same key belong in investigation, not silent replacement. Store raw authenticated evidence with restricted access and retain a normalized audit trail. Paid commission later reversed becomes a recoverable debit or an offset against future payouts, according to the contract. Reconcile those offsets against statements so the ledger does not report cash still available after the merchant has already recovered it from a subsequent settlement.

Upload only permitted conversion data and preserve the distinction between advertising attribution and accounting truth. Google offline conversion requests need a genuine captured GCLID, a configured conversion action, correctly zoned conversion time, value, currency, and a stable order identifier. Meta Conversions API does not accept FBCLID as an interchangeable Google-style identifier: preserve a legitimate click identifier through the documented fbc representation and send appropriate event metadata. Deduplicate browser and server copies with matching event names and event_id values. Inspect item-level responses, persist successful acknowledgments, and retry only transient failures. Google adjustments require the supported conversion adjustment workflow; a Meta refund event must not be assumed to retract a Purchase automatically. Maintain the financial reversal ledger regardless of platform support, and choose optimization signals whose timing and value do not knowingly overstate the economic outcome.

callout.title: S2S Postback, Ping-Post & Offline-Pixel Secrets
callout.body: Performance engineers prevent silent attribution black holes with four battle-tested S2S rules:
items: Capture `GCLID` / `MSCLKID` Into First-Party Server Storage on Landing, Not on Redirect: Visitors who use your fee calculator for 4 minutes or open 2 comparison tabs often lose URL query strings unless the landing page persists click tokens immediately.

Never Optimize Google/Meta Campaigns on Outbound Button Clicks: Bidding algorithms optimizing for cheap bridge clicks flood your funnel with curiosity bots; feed offline `Qualified Demo` / `Funded Account` S2S events discounted by your scrub rate.

Quarantine Unmatched `sub1` Webhooks Instead of Dropping Them: When a buyer shares a merchant checkout URL with a CFO on another device, `sub1` may return blank while the partner portal credits your vanity code—route null-`sub1` webhooks to a review table.

Enforce 800ms Ping Timeouts & Seller-Matched Consent Locks in Ping-Post: Slow downstream buyers tank quiz completion rates; cut off slow ping bidders at 800ms and never post PII unless the winning buyer matches the exact entity consented to by the user.

sections.heading: 3. Qualify, ping, post, and prove the handoff
paragraphs: The social_to_search_ping_post_arbitrage play starts with a four-step qualification quiz: service need, geography, eligibility, and preferred contact arrangement. Social creative must describe the actual service rather than promise an invented entitlement. The search bridge clarifies the visitor's intent before any lead auction occurs. Send a minimized ping containing only fields necessary to establish buyer eligibility and price; do not broadcast a complete contact record to every bidder. Even minimized fields can identify a person in combination, so review permitted sharing at the field level. Query only contracted buyers, impose response deadlines, and exclude buyers that cannot serve the declared need. A high bid from the wrong geography is not a usable offer. Record bid timestamps, eligibility decisions, and the routing policy version so rejected leads can be investigated without reconstructing the auction from memory.

Before releasing contact information, show the selected buyer's identity and requested contact channels, then capture explicit buyer-specific consent with the exact text version, timestamp, and relevant affirmative action. This is the operating design, not a claim that the TCPA universally requires this exact auction structure. Applicable requirements depend on the call or message and current rules. If the winning buyer changes after a timeout, do not silently transfer the existing permission to another buyer. Return to buyer selection and obtain permission for that recipient. Post the full lead only after the selected buyer remains eligible and the permission record matches. Use a stable lead identifier for retries, record acceptance separately from billing, and reconcile rejected duplicates and invalid numbers against the buyer's reason codes rather than treating every successful HTTP response as earned commission.

Run the ten checks below with synthetic fixtures before exposing paid traffic, then repeat the relevant checks whenever a merchant mapping or buyer contract changes. Measure scrub rates by buyer, creative, geography, and lead age; a blended acceptance rate hides a single bad route. Define a contact suppression mechanism shared across authorized outreach systems, and propagate withdrawal requests promptly under the applicable channel rules. For commercial email, maintain accurate sender information, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out; do not assume a purchased lead removes those duties. Preserve enough evidence to resolve billing disputes without keeping raw contact data indefinitely. The release artifact should contain fixture identifiers, expected outcomes, observed outcomes, and responsible owners. A checklist with ten green marks but no event records cannot distinguish a working integration from a person clicking through a form.

sections.heading: 4. Keep search-feed and web-checkout economics distinct
paragraphs: The tier1_search_feed_afd_rsoc_arbitrage play requires a genuine editorial destination, not a disguised collection of paid links. A compliant two-click Related Search on Content journey lets the visitor deliberately select a relevant related-search term, then independently choose a result on the provider's results page. Never force the second click, overlay controls, fabricate search intent, or pay people to click advertisements. Feed-provider keyword, placement, traffic-source, and click-intent rules govern the implementation; obtain the current written requirements rather than copying another publisher's layout. Keep RSOC separate from parked-domain or other feed products unless the provider expressly supports that configuration. Record editorial topic, approved term mapping, acquisition creative, and destination version. Investigate unusually high downstream click rates alongside session evidence and provider deductions, because a prettier revenue curve can simply be invalid traffic awaiting an eventual scrub adjustment.

The web2app_quiz_subscription_billing_bypass play is a partner web-acquisition arrangement, not permission to evade an app marketplace's rules. Partner with SaaS or mobile-app merchants that explicitly authorize external Stripe or Paddle web checkouts and the relevant geographic distribution path. Use a diagnostic quiz to recommend a suitable plan, with transparent recurring price, renewal cadence, trial conversion, and cancellation instructions before payment. The $40-$150 CPA range is an illustrative offer band for underwriting, not a verified universal payout. Confirm whether a qualifying event means checkout, first successful payment, retained subscriber, or a later validation milestone. Merchant GMV includes the customer's purchase value; affiliate commission includes only the contracted referral amount that survives reversals. Do not book annual subscription value as affiliate revenue or describe processor acceptance as proof that the subscriber will remain billable.

Use separate campaign namespaces for lead auctions, search-feed earnings, and subscription commissions. Their units are different: an accepted lead, a monetized search interaction, and a qualified subscription cannot share a conversion-rate denominator without misleading the operator. Report mature contribution per acquired visitor within each route, then compare equivalent time horizons and payout maturity. For subscriptions, include trial failures, refunds, chargebacks, and attribution disputes; for feeds, include invalid-traffic deductions; for leads, include duplicate and eligibility scrubs. Keep platform optimization events honest about what happened. A quiz completion is not a purchase, and a provisional purchase is not settled commission. The operator's intervention should target the failing stage rather than increasing traffic until volume hides it. Hold each route's budget steady when its latest cohort has not yet aged enough to support a credible comparison with prior cohorts.
